title: A double-quoted escape naming a lone surrogate code point
notes: Production [60] ns-esc-16-bit is an escaped 16-bit Unicode character. A surrogate code point (xD800 to xDFFF) is reserved for UTF-16 and encodes no character on its own: RFC 8259 section 8.2 calls a single unpaired surrogate escape a bit sequence that cannot encode a Unicode character, and a string holding one cannot be written in UTF-8, UTF-16 or UTF-32. YAML 1.2.2 does not settle it (section 5.2 counts every code point as a character, and leaving c-printable [1] does not make an escape invalid, as `\0` shows), so the kit refuses the escape as a convention. Loose mode needs any error; strict needs the syntax category, as for other refused escapes. This case says nothing about an escaped surrogate pair: a lone surrogate is refused whatever a library does with pairs.

provenance.reference: A decoder that turned a \u escape of a lone surrogate into a value (an invalid string or a replacement character) instead of refusing the escape.
